panel.summary: Unbounded `value.toUpperCase()` on the per-repaint render path over attacker/collaborator-controlled cell text
panel.evidence: `isCheckboxChecked` is called once per visible checkbox per repaint from `gridcanvas.ts:1042` with the raw cell value (`cell?.v`). The new fallback at data-validation.ts:166 short-circuits only on the exact strings `TRUE`/`FALSE`; every other value now allocates a full uppercased copy of the string on each frame. Cell values are not length-bounded anywhere I could find in packages/sheets (no MaxCell/maxLength constant), and they can be supplied by a remote collaborator (Yorkie doc), an xlsx import, or a paste — the very sources this change cites as motivation. A peer who writes a multi-megabyte string into a cell covered by a checkbox rule causes a per-frame O(n) allocation + case-map in the other participants' render loop (jank / memory churn), where the pre-change code did a length-short-circuited `===`. Impact is client-side resource consumption only, not data exposure; I did not build a PoC, hence low confidence. A length guard (e.g. skip the fallback when `value.length > CHECKBOX_TRUE.length`) removes the vector entirely, since no value longer than 5 chars can uppercase to `TRUE`.
